text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: it costs x to take the y test.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provide(x, y) ::: x provides y.
Applicant(x, y) ::: x is a y applicant.
Hardship(x) ::: x can prove economic hardship.
Family(x, y) ::: x lives in a y family.
Resource(x, y) ::: x has y resources available to them.
Premises:
Cost(205, gre) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Applicant(x, gre) ∧ Hardship(x) → Provide(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (Family(x, singleparent) ∨ Resource(x, few) → Hardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
Family(tom, singleparent) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Resource(tom, few) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Applicant(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Provide(ets, tom) ::: ETS provides financial aid to Tom.
